title: Supercritical fluid of quantum electrons in three-dimensional superconducting fullerides
authors: Xinying Li, Yuki Matsuda, Chongli Yang, Huaxue Zhou, Takuma Ogasawara, Qin Wang, Liguo Zhang, Hidekazu Shimotani, Hailiang Xia, Khuong K. Huynh, Panagiotis Kotetes, Satoshi Heguri, Katsumi Tanigaki
abstract: The supercritical fluid (SCF) of quantum electrons at the Mott metal-insulator transition without symmetry breaking is one of the most elusive phenomena in strongly correlated electron physics. Prior studies of Cr-doped V2O3 and organic Mott systems reported discrepant critical exponents. A key limitation is that the scaling analysis relies on a single experimental observable, leaving the roles of phase coexistence, inhomogeneity, and percolation unaddressed. Here we report the first experimental identification of a thermodynamically equilibrated SCF phase and its associated Mott endpoint in the three-dimensional superconducting fullerides CsxRb3-xC60, using two independent probes of electrical conductivity and magnetic susceptibility, which reveal two distinct metal-insulator transition lines converging at a single Mott endpoint. A hypothesis-free two-particle analysis of magnetic susceptibilities yields a metal-insulator coexisting SCF by exhibiting the maximum two-phase mixing entropy, in agreement with a picture of a thermodynamically equilibrated Widom line. Simultaneously, conductivity scaling yields a critical exponent in the regime of quantum critical predictions. Our new dual-probe approach provides a unified microscopic picture of the Mott SCF with a characteristic length scale below current diffraction resolution, in addition to a new interpretation on the origin of superconducting Tc-dome.
summary: This work reports the first experimental evidence for a thermodynamically equilibrated Supercritical Fluid (SCF) phase at the Mott transition in superconducting fullerides. By simultaneously analyzing electrical conductivity and magnetic susceptibility, the authors establish two distinct but converging MIT lines meeting at a Mott endpoint. This dual-probe approach provides a unified picture of the correlated electron physics underlying high-$T_c$ superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates the elusive supercritical fluid (SCF) phase of quantum electrons at the Mott metal-insulator transition (MIT) in strongly correlated systems without symmetry breaking.
main_result: The authors report the first experimental identification of a thermodynamically equilibrated SCF phase and its associated Mott endpoint using superconducting fullerides, unifying insights from both electrical conductivity and magnetic susceptibility measurements.
method: A dual-probe approach combining independent measurements of electrical conductivity ($\sigma$) and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), along with hypothesis-free two-particle analysis (Widom line) and scaling analysis, was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is the three-dimensional superconducting fulleride $	ext{Cs}_x	ext{Rb}_{3-x}	ext{C}_{60}$. Theoretical modeling involves effective spin Hamiltonians and analyzing electronic state degeneracies related to $t_{1u}$-orbitals.
key_observables:
Electrical conductivity ($\sigma$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), critical exponents ($z
u$), Mott endpoint (MEP), and the superconducting $	ext{T}_c$-dome structure.
important_parameters: Stoichiometry ($x$ in $	ext{Cs}_x	ext{Rb}_{3-x}	ext{C}_{60}$), temperature ($T$), pressure ($P$), and unit cell volume ($V_{	ext{cell}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a thermodynamically equilibrated SCF phase, which is characterized by maximizing two-phase mixing entropy in magnetic susceptibility measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the convergence of distinct MIT lines from $\sigma$ and $\chi$ at an MEP, mapping out the SCF zone on T-V diagrams, and comparing theoretical models to experimental data across various stoichiometries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical problem (SCF at Mott transition), then presenting the dual-probe methodology using fullerides, analyzing both $\sigma$ and $\chi$ measurements independently, and finally synthesizing these results into a unified microscopic picture of the M-I coexisting SCF phase.
why_interesting: The rigorous combination of transport ($\sigma$) and magnetic ($\chi$) probes to characterize a single quantum critical point provides a powerful methodology for studying strongly correlated electron physics that transcends limitations of single-observable analyses.
